items.front: Ripon's Resolution 1882 — why is it landmark?
items.back: Called the 'Magna Carta of local self-government'; introduced elected members and non-official chairpersons. Mayo's 1870 Resolution began financial decentralisation.

items.front: Committees on Panchayati Raj — who recommended what?
items.back: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957): three-tier PRI; Ashok Mehta (1977): two-tier; G.V.K. Rao (1985): district as planning unit; L.M. Singhvi (1986): constitutional status.
items.examPoint: Committees — Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, Singhvi

items.back: Rajasthan — 2 Oct 1959 (Nagaur), followed by Andhra Pradesh (1 Nov 1959). Article 40 (DPSP) had directed organising village panchayats.
Part IX ('The Panchayats'), Arts 243–243O, Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects); in force 24 April 1993 (National Panchayati Raj Day).
Part IXA ('The Municipalities'), Arts 243P–243ZG, Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects); in force 1 June 1993.
Village (Gram Panchayat) → Intermediate (Block/Mandal) → District (Zilla Parishad); Art 243B — intermediate tier optional for States with population ≤ 20 lakh.
Art 243D: SC/ST in proportion to population; women ≥ one-third (many States 50%). Minimum age to be a member = 21 (Art 243F), NOT 25.
items.examPoint: Minimum age (21) & tenure of Panchayat members (Art 243E/243F)

items.front: SEC vs SFC — articles and roles?
items.back: State Election Commission (Art 243K) conducts panchayat/municipal elections (NOT the ECI). State Finance Commission (Art 243I) reviews local-body finances every 5 years.
items.examPoint: State Election Commission (243K) & State Finance Commission (243I)

items.back: The body of ALL registered voters of a village; its powers are decided by the State Legislature. It is the base deliberative unit of the panchayat system.

items.front: PESA 1996 — what does it do (and its objective trap)?
items.back: Extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule (Scheduled) areas in 10 states (incl. AP); empowers Gram Sabha over minor forest produce/land/water. Objective = self-governance, NOT creating autonomous regions.
items.examPoint: PESA 1996 — Fifth Schedule; Gram Sabha empowerment

items.back: Nagar Panchayat (transitional area) → Municipal Council (smaller) → Municipal Corporation (larger, headed by a Mayor). DPC (243ZD) & MPC (243ZE) integrate area plans.

items.front: AP local government — PR Act & mandal tier?
items.back: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 implemented the 73rd Amendment; tiers = Gram Panchayat (Sarpanch) → Mandal Praja Parishad → Zilla Praja Parishad. Mandal introduced under N.T. Rama Rao (1980s).
Launched 2 Oct 2019 for doorstep governance; ~15,004 Grama + 3,842 Ward Sachivalayams; backed by Volunteers each serving ~50 households. Administrative — does NOT replace the Gram Sabha.
Uses drones to survey abadi (inhabited) rural land and issues property cards (record of rights); run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj; eases credit access and cuts land disputes.
items.examPoint: SVAMITVA scheme — property cards via drone survey (Ministry of Panchayati Raj)
